status: explicit spin-2 propagator and completion-cost audit beyond finite local curvature-square truncations

conventions.momentum: Euclidean p^2 is used to display zeros; a pole at p^2=-m^2 is a Lorentzian mass m
conventions.scope: spin-2 transverse-traceless projector and positive overall Planck normalization are suppressed
conventions.health: a simple real pole is healthy when its diagonalized kinetic mode has positive norm; complex poles fail ordinary spectral unitarity

poles.interpretation: massive spin-2 ghost under ordinary Feynman quantization

entireCompletion.zeroFreeReason: the complex exponential is entire and never zero at finite argument
entireCompletion.decision: the massless Einstein pole survives and no additional spin-2 particle or gap is generated

polynomialSequence.firstOrder: P_1=1+x gives residues +1 at x=0 and -1 at x=-1
polynomialSequence.decision: every nonconstant finite Taylor truncation has extra propagator poles; even orders have complex-conjugate poles and odd orders also have one real negative root in the checked sequence
polynomialSequence.interpretation: the extra poles do not converge to additional poles of exp(x); they are truncation artifacts that move through the complex plane as N changes

bimetricCompletion.linearTTKernel: K=[[p^2+mu^2,-mu^2],[-mu^2,p^2+mu^2]] for two canonically normalized positive-kinetic spin-2 fields
bimetricCompletion.nonlinearCondition: the Hassan-Rosen square-root potential and its secondary constraint are required to remove the Boulware-Deser scalar
bimetricCompletion.decision: unlike a one-field four-derivative propagator, the full two-field theory can have positive residues at both poles

bimetricDerivativeExpansion.firstTruncation: K_eff^(1)=2p^2(1-p^2/m_2^2), which has an additional truncation pole at p^2=+m_2^2
bimetricDerivativeExpansion.warning: the derivative expansion is valid only below the massive pole/series singularity; resumming a finite curvature-square truncation as fundamental invents a ghost or tachyon not present in the positive-residue two-field spectrum
bimetricDerivativeExpansion.literatureMap: integrating one metric out of ghost-free bimetric theory produces an infinite higher-curvature action; the apparent higher-derivative ghost of finite truncations is not a pole of the full bimetric theory

entireNonlocal: requires a covariant entire function of derivative operators, a contour/prescription and a specified function space
absence of extra free poles does not by itself prove microcausality, reflection positivity, nonlinear stability or a well-posed global initial-value problem
loop self-energies contain logarithms and branch cuts and need not preserve the chosen zero-free entire form without a UV symmetry or completion
the exponential example has no healthy gapped massive spin-2 pole; it only preserves the Einstein pole
bimetric: adds a second vierbein/metric and five physical massive-spin-2 degrees of freedom
requires the tuned Hassan-Rosen/dRGT interaction potential and a matter-coupling choice that preserves the constraint below the cutoff
has a strong-coupling/Vainshtein scale and background-dependent stability and characteristic cones that require separate checks
radiative corrections and generic composite matter couplings can detune the special potential or reintroduce the Boulware-Deser mode above an EFT scale
spin23Parent: the single Spin(2,3) connection and selector do not supply either an entire covariant form factor or a second metric
the nonlocal route needs an infinite tower F(D^2/M^2) with ordering and gauge-covariance data
the bimetric route needs a second vierbein/Spin connection or a derived composite metric and an explanation of the square-root potential
neither spin-2 escape repairs the axial 1-plus/0-minus sign no-go of claim 1615; the torsion sector still needs a decoupling or critical completion

decision: Both principal escapes invalidate the inference that every curvature-square coefficient implies a physical spin-2 ghost. A zero-free entire form factor keeps only the healthy massless graviton, while full ghost-free bimetric theory has a healthy massless graviton plus a gapped five-polarization spin-2 mode. Neither follows from the current broken Spin(2,3) parent: nonlocality imports an infinite functional choice and bimetric theory imports a second metric plus a tuned constraint-preserving potential.
stopRules: Do not infer poles of an entire or bimetric completion from a finite derivative truncation beyond its convergence/cutoff domain.
Do not call a zero-free entire propagator a mass-gap mechanism: it has no added massive pole.
Do not call a generic two-metric potential ghost-free; require the Hassan-Rosen constraint structure.
Do not couple matter generically to both metrics without rechecking the Boulware-Deser constraint and EFT cutoff.
Do not claim a Spin(2,3) completion until the entire operator or second metric and interaction potential are derived from explicit parent variables.
Retain claim 1615 independently: these are spin-2 completions, not a cure of the axial torsion sign contradiction.
